column1: # The userspace smoke scenario — what a user would call working, in one place.
#   cargo xtask smoke <log> <seconds> <qemu command…>      (the three arches)
#   node tools/wasm-browser/run.js                               (wasm)
# One step per line: the command, a tab, and the line its output must produce. An empty expectation
# means the step has nothing to say and the next prompt is the whole of its evidence — a write.
# Two rules, both of them cause (h) in .notes/test_gates.md:
#   * The expectation is matched against a *whole line*. The guest echoes what it is sent, so
#     `# /bin/echo smoke-ok` would satisfy a substring search for `smoke-ok` on a shell that
#     echoed the line and never ran the command. Anchored, only the output can satisfy it.
#   * The expectation is therefore never a prefix or substring of its own command.
# Why these steps: they are the ones that need the file-backed exec path (an image binary
# exec'd by the shell), the filesystem (a file created, and read back through a second open), a
# second process, which is what was broken, invisibly, when init stopped at `RTS_PAGEFAULT`
# (finding 57), and a server that answers a path from its own in-memory tree (`/proc`). `boot.cjs`
# and `page.test.js` assert much more on wasm; this is the part every target can be asked, and wasm
# cannot answer for the other three: it has no page faults, so it never runs FDIO or the
# demand-paged path at all.
# The `/proc` step's answer must not depend on the clock, so the value is thrown away and only the
# second command's line is asserted. A procfs read that faults stops the system, and the step then
# has no answer at all; that is the failure it is here to catch (the wasm system trapped on
# `cat /proc/hz` because its file-handler tag was a low bit that collided with a function index).
/bin/echo smoke-ok
/bin/echo hello-from-the-image > smoke.txt
/bin/cat smoke.txt
/bin/cat /proc/hz > /dev/null && /bin/echo procfs-ok
